Heparin Calcium (BANM) Calcium Heparin; Hepariinikalsium; Heparin Kalsiyum; Heparin Sodyum; Heparin vápenatá sůl; Heparina cálcica; Héparine cal- cique; Heparinkalcium; Heparino kalcio druska; Heparinum calci- cum; Heparyna wapniowa. CAS — 37270-89-6. ATC — B01AB01; C05BA03; S01XA14. ATC Vet — QB01AB01; QC05BA03; QS01XA14. Pharmacopoeias. In Eur. (see p.vii), Int., and US. Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Heparin Calcium). The potency of heparin calcium intended for parenteral use is not less than 150 international units per mg and the potency of heparin calcium not intended for parenteral use is not less than 120 international units per mg, both calculated with reference to the dried substance. A white or al- most white, hygroscopic powder. Freely soluble in water. A 1% solution in water has a pH of 5.5 to 8.0. Store in airtight contain- ers. USP 31 (Heparin Calcium). The calcium salt of heparin with a potency, calculated on the dried basis, of not less than 140 USP units in each mg. USP heparin units are not equivalent to inter- national units. The source of the material is usually the intestinal mucosa or other suitable tissues of domestic mammals used for food by man and should be stated on the label. A 1% solution in water has a pH of 5.0 to 7.5. Store in airtight containers at tem- peratures below 40°, preferably between 15 and 30°. Incompatibility. See Heparin Sodium, below. Heparin Sodium (BANM, rINN) Hepariininatrium; Heparin sodná sůl; Heparina sódica; Héparine sodique; Heparinnatrium; Heparino natrio druska; Heparinum natricum; Heparyna sodowa; Sodium Heparin; Soluble Heparin. Гепарин Натрий CAS — 9041-08-1. ATC — B01AB01; C05BA03; S01XA14. ATC Vet — QB01AB01; QC05BA03; QS01XA14. Pharmacopoeias. In Chin., Eur. (see p.vii), Int., Jpn, and US. Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Heparin Sodium). The potency of heparin sodium intended for parenteral use is not less than 150 international units per mg and the potency of heparin sodium not intended for parenteral use is not less than 120 international units per mg, both calculated with reference to the dried substance. A white or al- most white, hygroscopic powder. Freely soluble in water. A 1% solution in water has a pH of 5.5 to 8.0.
